assumptions: Finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel E, including rank zero; alpha,beta are nonnegative.
Six original analytic assumptions: alpha>0, alpha<=beta, V is C2, alpha||v||^2<=D2V(x)[v,v]<=beta||v||^2 for all x,v, eta>0, beta*eta<=1.
All y,r,z0, finite n and T>=0, and all strictly ordered prescribed event tuples are universally quantified.
Flow, reflection, rate, integrated arc hazard, tagged histories, finite interpolation and density are explicit definitions inherited literally from the actual finite-count law.
Integrability and incoming left limits are conclusions. No continuity of the reflection at a vanishing normal, positive density, supplied path law or stochastic independence premise is added.
units.statement:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space equipped with its Borel sigma algebra; zero dimension is allowed. Let alpha,beta>=0, eta be real, V:E->R. Assume exactly alpha>0, alpha<=beta, V is C2, alpha||v||^2<=D2V(x)[v,v]<=beta||v||^2 for every x,v, eta>0 and beta*eta<=1. All conclusions hold for every y,r in E, initial phase z0=(x0,p0), integer n>=0 and finite T>=0.
Set c=y-eta*grad V(r). For z=(x,p), define Phi_u(z)=(c+cos(u)(x-c)+sqrt(eta)sin(u)p, -sin(u)/sqrt(eta)(x-c)+cos(u)p). Define h_r(x)=grad V(x)-grad V(r), S_r(x,p)=(x,p-[2<p,h_r(x)>/||h_r(x)||^2]h_r(x)) with real division totalized by 0/0=0, lambda_r(x,p)=sqrt(eta)max(0,<p,h_r(x)>), and Lambda_z(u)=integral from0 to u of lambda_r(Phi_s(z)) ds for u>=0, using Lebesgue measure.
A tagged record is either live(a,z), with a>=0, or stopped; Hist_n is the type of all n+1 records. Let Delta_n(T) be the strict simplex 0<t1<...<tn<T. Write a0=0, ai=ti (1<=i<=n), a_(n+1)=T. Given t in Delta_n(T), define z_i=S_r(Phi_(a_i-a_(i-1))(z_(i-1))) for1<=i<=n and K_n(t)_j=live(a_j,z_j). The literal Lean nonnegative conversions preserve these nonnegative times. Define qReal_n(t)=product_(i=1)^n [lambda_r(Phi_(a_i-a_(i-1))(z_(i-1))) exp(-Lambda_(z_(i-1))(a_i-a_(i-1)))], q_n=ofReal(qReal_n).
For arbitrary histories let readTime(live(a,z))=a and readTime(stopped)=0; d_n(T,h)=max(T-readTime(h_n),0). Put W(live(a,z),u)=ofReal(exp(-Lambda_z(u))) and W(stopped,u)=0. Define rho_n(T,t)=q_n(t) W(K_n(t)_n,d_n(T,K_n(t))). Here ofReal(x) is max(x,0) embedded into extended nonnegative reals; no probability law or normalization is assumed in this deterministic identity.
Define Path_T as all phase-valued functions on[0,T]. The total interpolation Psi_n(h)(s) starts at z0 and scans records j=0,...,n in order: a live(a,z) record with a<=s replaces the accumulator by Phi_(max(s-a,0))(z); otherwise it is unchanged. Set Gamma_n(t)=Psi_n(K_n(t)). Extend this particular prescribed path to all real times by gamma(s)=Gamma_n(t)(min(max(s,0),T)). This extension agrees with Gamma on[0,T]; no topology on an entire function space is asserted.
Then lambda_r(gamma(s)) is Lebesgue interval integrable on[0,T], and integral_0^T lambda_r(gamma(s)) ds=sum_(j=0)^n Lambda_(z_j)(a_(j+1)-a_j). For every1<=i<=n, gamma(s) tends from the left at a_i to Phi_(a_i-a_(i-1))(z_(i-1)), and lambda_r(gamma(s)) tends from the left to lambda_r of that same incoming phase. Consequently rho_n(T,t)=ofReal(exp(-integral_0^T lambda_r(gamma(s))ds) * product_(i=1)^n lambda_r(Phi_(a_i-a_(i-1))(z_(i-1)))). The density evaluates the incoming phase, not the reflected value at the jump.
These conclusions include n=0 (one survival arc, empty product1), T=0 (only the zero-event simplex is inhabited), zero-dimensional E and zero rates; no positivity of event densities is assumed. All integrability, continuity along arcs, left limits and identities are proved, not additional premises.
This is an attributed ASTIS completion of the prescribed-trajectory hazard/left-limit ingredient of Appendix A.1 around(A.7), not a quoted standalone theorem. Composing it with the finite-count path law, summing over all counts, signed-observable convergence, Skorokhod compatibility, restart/Markovness, invariance, hypocoercivity, implementation errors, unbounded expected costs and the main paper/composition results remain separate obligations.

steps.title: Ignore endpoint values only for integration
steps.text: Assume a<=b. A continuous comparison function g is integrable on every finite interval. If f=g on the open interval(a,b), changing the two endpoint values does not change Lebesgue interval integrability or its integral. Transfer integrability with congr_uIoo and the integral with integral_congr_Ioo_of_le. The a=b case is included; no equality or continuity at a jump is required.

private theorem arc_integral {f g : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b)
    (hg : Continuous g) (heq : EqOn f g (Ioo a b)) :
    IntervalIntegrable f volume a b ∧
      (∫ s in a..b, f s) = ∫ s in a..b, g s := by
  refine ⟨(hg.intervalIntegrable a b).congr_uIoo ?_,
    intervalIntegral.integral_congr_Ioo_of_le hab heq⟩
  rw [uIoo_of_le hab]
  exact heq.symm

steps.title: Sum the finite adjacent integrals
steps.text: Let the grid be nondecreasing; for every j assume g_j is continuous and f=g_j on(a_j,a_(j+1)). Induct on the number of grid intervals. The zero-interval integral and empty sum vanish. At the successor step, integrability of the prefix and last arc gives integrability of their union. The adjacent-interval identity adds the last integral, and the finite sum splits into its prefix and last index. This proves the exact sum for any nondecreasing finite grid without requiring positive lengths.

private theorem finite_arc_integral (n : ℕ) (a : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ)
    (f : ℝ → ℝ) (g : Fin n → ℝ → ℝ) (ha : Monotone a)
    (hg : ∀ j, Continuous (g j))
    (heq : ∀ j, EqOn f (g j) (Ioo (a j.castSucc) (a j.succ))) :
    IntervalIntegrable f volume (a 0) (a (Fin.last n)) ∧
      (∫ s in a 0..a (Fin.last n), f s) =
        ∑ j : Fin n, ∫ s in a j.castSucc..a j.succ, g j s := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
    have hpre := ih (fun j => a j.castSucc) (fun j => g j.castSucc)
      (fun i j hij => ha (by simpa using hij)) (fun j => hg j.castSucc)
      (fun j => by simpa using heq j.castSucc)
    have hlast := arc_integral (ha (Fin.castSucc_le_succ (Fin.last n)))
      (hg (Fin.last n)) (heq (Fin.last n))
    refine ⟨hpre.1.trans hlast.1, ?_⟩
    rw [Fin.sum_univ_castSucc]
    simp only [Fin.succ_castSucc]
    rw [← hpre.2, ← hlast.2]
    exact (intervalIntegral.integral_add_adjacent_intervals hpre.1 hlast.1).symm

steps.title: Determine an incoming limit from the preceding arc

units.lean_statement:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space equipped with its Borel sigma algebra; zero dimension is allowed. Let alpha,beta>=0, eta be real, V:E->R. Assume exactly alpha>0, alpha<=beta, V is C2, alpha||v||^2<=D2V(x)[v,v]<=beta||v||^2 for every x,v, eta>0 and beta*eta<=1. All conclusions hold for every y,r in E, initial phase z0=(x0,p0), integer n>=0 and finite T>=0.
Set c=y-eta*grad V(r). For z=(x,p), define Phi_u(z)=(c+cos(u)(x-c)+sqrt(eta)sin(u)p, -sin(u)/sqrt(eta)(x-c)+cos(u)p). Define h_r(x)=grad V(x)-grad V(r), S_r(x,p)=(x,p-[2<p,h_r(x)>/||h_r(x)||^2]h_r(x)) with real division totalized by 0/0=0, lambda_r(x,p)=sqrt(eta)max(0,<p,h_r(x)>), and Lambda_z(u)=integral from0 to u of lambda_r(Phi_s(z)) ds for u>=0, using Lebesgue measure.
A tagged record is either live(a,z), with a>=0, or stopped; Hist_n is the type of all n+1 records. Let Delta_n(T) be the strict simplex 0<t1<...<tn<T. Write a0=0, ai=ti (1<=i<=n), a_(n+1)=T. Given t in Delta_n(T), define z_i=S_r(Phi_(a_i-a_(i-1))(z_(i-1))) for1<=i<=n and K_n(t)_j=live(a_j,z_j). The literal Lean nonnegative conversions preserve these nonnegative times. Define qReal_n(t)=product_(i=1)^n [lambda_r(Phi_(a_i-a_(i-1))(z_(i-1))) exp(-Lambda_(z_(i-1))(a_i-a_(i-1)))], q_n=ofReal(qReal_n).
For arbitrary histories let readTime(live(a,z))=a and readTime(stopped)=0; d_n(T,h)=max(T-readTime(h_n),0). Put W(live(a,z),u)=ofReal(exp(-Lambda_z(u))) and W(stopped,u)=0. Define rho_n(T,t)=q_n(t) W(K_n(t)_n,d_n(T,K_n(t))). Here ofReal(x) is max(x,0) embedded into extended nonnegative reals; no probability law or normalization is assumed in this deterministic identity.
Define Path_T as all phase-valued functions on[0,T]. The total interpolation Psi_n(h)(s) starts at z0 and scans records j=0,...,n in order: a live(a,z) record with a<=s replaces the accumulator by Phi_(max(s-a,0))(z); otherwise it is unchanged. Set Gamma_n(t)=Psi_n(K_n(t)). Extend this particular prescribed path to all real times by gamma(s)=Gamma_n(t)(min(max(s,0),T)). This extension agrees with Gamma on[0,T]; no topology on an entire function space is asserted.
Then lambda_r(gamma(s)) is Lebesgue interval integrable on[0,T], and integral_0^T lambda_r(gamma(s)) ds=sum_(j=0)^n Lambda_(z_j)(a_(j+1)-a_j). For every1<=i<=n, gamma(s) tends from the left at a_i to Phi_(a_i-a_(i-1))(z_(i-1)), and lambda_r(gamma(s)) tends from the left to lambda_r of that same incoming phase. Consequently rho_n(T,t)=ofReal(exp(-integral_0^T lambda_r(gamma(s))ds) * product_(i=1)^n lambda_r(Phi_(a_i-a_(i-1))(z_(i-1)))). The density evaluates the incoming phase, not the reflected value at the jump.
These conclusions include n=0 (one survival arc, empty product1), T=0 (only the zero-event simplex is inhabited), zero-dimensional E and zero rates; no positivity of event densities is assumed. All integrability, continuity along arcs, left limits and identities are proved, not additional premises.
This is an attributed ASTIS completion of the prescribed-trajectory hazard/left-limit ingredient of Appendix A.1 around(A.7), not a quoted standalone theorem. Composing it with the finite-count path law, summing over all counts, signed-observable convergence, Skorokhod compatibility, restart/Markovness, invariance, hypocoercivity, implementation errors, unbounded expected costs and the main paper/composition results remain separate obligations.
